## Design

### 2026-10-11: First worked on the schematic, which was probably the easier part of the whole thing. Learned how to add symbols, connect things with wires, and labels.

**2.38h**

First worked on the schematic, which was probably the easier part of the whole thing. Learned how to add symbols, connect things with wires, and labels.

Then worked on the PCB, which was a lot more annoying. I had to redo the traces so many times cause I kept getting confused and getting errors with the Design Rule Checker. Learned that traces just follow from the thin blue lines already present and that traces cannot cross (which is why you use the front and back layers). V to add vias to switch between front and back. Also added drawings which was pretty fun.

Next Steps: Clear out my storage so that I can download the esp32 library thing in Arduino IDE and then do more.

### 2026-10-11: Day 2 of Starbie:

**2h**

Day 2 of Starbie:

Today, I worked on the firmware, which was relatively straightforward since it was mostly copy paste. Besides drawing sparkles, I added a drawing something method that will draw something like a square. After that,  I worked on the gerbers file, which was relatively straightforward with a youtube tutorial. Basically, you just have to adjust the settings according to the manufacturer (in this case, jlcpcb).

Then, I worked on the version control, which was kind of annoying. It's been a while since I last used github so I had to search a lot up, like how to create a repo and cloning to local machine. I added the firmware folder and I also added the PCB files. I got confused on how to add the PCB files to the repo, but what I did was to go to KiCAD project files, right click to open the project in finder, and then drag the folder into my repo folder (which could be found under github folder). So that worked pretty well. Then, I noticed that some history file keeps getting update, so I searched online and it turns out that I should be adding a .gitignore file. Adding the .gitignore file was kind of annoying, but what I did was open textedit, create a file as plaintext, and copy paste the code. Then, because finder automatically hides files that start with a period, I had to do cmd + shift + period to reveal the file in Desktop, and then drag it into my PCB folder. I also had to make sure that the file wasn't a txt file, so I had to do cmd + i because finder hides the extension, and then edit the name there.

After that, I worked on the README.md. I tried working on it in VScode, but I got confused on how to add images, so i just decided to work on it in GitHub directly. To add images, drag and drop from finder and then it automatically adds a url. Then, I worked on the BOM and created a BOM.csv file using Google Sheets (basically create a table in google sheets and then export as .csv).

Next Steps: put in some of my ideas so that it's not copy paste and prob change up the BOM.

### 2026-10-11: Day 2 of Starbie (cont):

**4.88h**

Day 2 of Starbie (cont):

So I did some more stuff and added some custom features.
1. added a buzzer to play music. adding this to the schematic was relatively straightforward since it was just putting in a buzzer symbol and then connecting it to an empty pin in the esp 32 and connecting negative to GND. the more annoying part was rerouting the PCB since i kept having to changing the layout of the components since there were too many intersections.
2. i tried to understand the original code and i get most of it but not the specific details. things i learned: enums for the reactions, struct is kind of like a class (has a bunch of variables in like an object), you can create an array of those "objects," use deadzones since things can't be exactly 0, use of millis() for time keeping, preferences help remember + store data, + lots more.
3. music playing code. create a pitches.h file to store the notes and then create a melody and duration parallel array. then, in a music playing function, check if the music is playing and if the sprite is sleeping. if both are true, return. then, if the song is not playing, set the song is playing boolean to be true. if the note is still playing (current timecertain threshold, then the animation would appear.

Some takeaways:
*make sure to know the exact type of component you're using when designing the pcb. i used a different type of piezo buzzer from what i found online, so i had to change that and reroute the pcb for the 50th time.

next steps: add some more animations, add sound for selection.
